facts.text: On this date in 1881, the Gunfight at the O.K. Corral lasted roughly 30 seconds — yet it defined the mythology of the American West for the next century and a half.
On this date in 1994, Jordan and Israel signed a formal peace treaty, making Jordan only the second Arab country ever to normalize relations with Israel.
More people live inside a circle drawn around Dhaka, Bangladesh than inside one of the same size drawn around Tokyo — Dhaka's density is simply without modern parallel.
Canada has more lakes than every other country on Earth combined, holding roughly 60% of the world's fresh surface lake water within its borders.
The city of Istanbul sits on two continents simultaneously — roughly 97% of Turkey's land is in Asia, yet its largest city and cultural capital straddles Europe and Asia across the Bosphorus.
On this day in 1929, the week after Black Thursday, the Dow posted its largest single-day gain to that point — markets often surge hardest in the middle of crashes.
On Oct 26, 1984, Eurotunnel was incorporated. It would become one of history's most catastrophic IPOs, losing investors roughly 94% of their money over a decade.
The S&P 500 has historically risen more in the final two months of the year than in the other ten combined — a pattern consistent enough to have its own name: the Santa Claus rally.
Saudi Aramco briefly surpassed $2 trillion in market cap in 2019, making it worth more than Google, Amazon, and Facebook combined at the time.
The Dutch East India Company paid an uninterrupted dividend for nearly 200 years — a streak no modern corporation has come close to matching.
On this date in 1958, the first commercial jet service across the Atlantic launched. The aircraft flew at 35,000 feet where the outside air is -60°C — colder than anywhere on Earth's surface.
Your bones are not inert scaffolding. They secrete a hormone called osteocalcin that regulates memory, fertility, and stress response, making the skeleton an active endocrine organ.
A neutron star packs more mass than the Sun into a sphere the size of a city. A single teaspoon of its material would weigh about a billion tons on Earth.
On October 26, 1977, the last naturally occurring smallpox case was recorded in Somalia. The virus had killed an estimated 300 million people in the 20th century alone.
The human eye can detect a single photon of light in total darkness. Your visual system is not limited by biology — it is limited only by the quantum nature of light itself.
On this day in 1825, the Erie Canal opened — making New York City the dominant American port. The canal is older than the photograph, the postage stamp, and the word 'scientist.'
Oxford University was already 300 years old when the Aztec Empire was founded. Medieval Europe and pre-Columbian America existed in the same century.
On this day in 1881, the Gunfight at the O.K. Corral lasted roughly 30 seconds. It became the most mythologized 30 seconds in American history only after Hollywood needed a creation story.
Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the construction of the Great Pyramid. She was an archaeologist's contemporary, not a pyramid builder's.
The fax machine was invented before the American Civil War. Businesses were transmitting documents over wires in 1843 while Abraham Lincoln was still a country lawyer in Illinois.
Vellichor (n.): the strange wistfulness of used bookshops. Coined by John Koenig in *The Dictionary of Obscure Sorrows* — proof that naming a feeling is halfway to owning it.
Sonder (n.): the realization that every passerby has a life as vivid and complex as your own. Another Koenig coinage, now used seriously by people who've forgotten it was invented in 2012.

On this day in 1825, the Erie Canal opened, and Americans suddenly needed a word for the fever it triggered: *canal mania*. English has always built compound nouns as fast as it builds infrastructure.
Mamihlapinatapai: a Yaghan word for the look shared by two people who both want something but neither will initiate. The language has fewer than a handful of speakers left; the look is universal.
On this day in 1881, the Gunfight at the O.K. Corral lasted 30 seconds. The word *gunfight* itself didn't appear in print until years later — English named the myth long after the moment passed.
On this date in 2021, Bitcoin hit $60,000 for the first time after the ProShares BITO ETF launched — the fastest ETF to reach $1B AUM in history, doing so in two days.

On this date in 2016, the Ethereum network processed block 2,463,000 during the height of the Shanghai DoS attacks, when an attacker exploited EXTCODESIZE for roughly $1 per 50,000 forced node operations.
Bitcoin's UTXO model means your wallet balance doesn't exist — only discrete unspent outputs do. Your "balance" is software fiction layered over a ledger of discrete coins.
Satoshi's genesis block coinbase contains the text 'The Times 03/Jan/2009 Chancellor on brink of second bailout for banks' — both a timestamp and an editorial, embedded permanently in the chain.
The DAO hack in 2016 drained 3.6M ETH through a reentrancy bug — the attacker couldn't immediately spend it due to a 28-day withdrawal lock, giving Ethereum time to execute the hard fork.
On this date in 2015, Microsoft's ResNet-152 surpassed human-level accuracy on ImageNet for the first time — a benchmark researchers had assumed would take another decade to fall.
On this date in 2017, Google Brain published the Transformer paper. Every major language model running today is a direct architectural descendant of those eight pages.
GPT-4's training run is estimated to have consumed roughly 50 GWh of electricity — comparable to the annual consumption of 4,500 average U.S. households.
AlphaFold 2 predicted structures for over 200 million proteins in 2022, more than all experimental structures accumulated by humanity in the prior 70 years of structural biology.
The first neural network to beat a professional Go player, AlphaGo, defeated Fan Hui in October 2015 — a milestone the field had projected was at least a decade away.
